text:
maya: heads up — a few customers on ap-southeast reported websocket 1006 closes right after tiny payloads. Repro shows server sending many ~20-40 byte frames and the client lib treats one as EOF then reconnects.

diego: are these compressed chunks or plain text?

maya: some are gzip-chunked at the http2 layer; packet capture: `1f8b0800...7b226b223a22x22` corresponds to compressed JSON `{\"k\":\"\"}` but arriving as micro-writes.

ellen: we toggled http2 flush in last proxy rollout, that could explain it. Two paths: revert aggressive-flush or coalesce tiny writes at the proxy. Revert might reduce perf elsewhere.

diego: proposal: add proxy flag `coalesce_small_frames=true` default off. Heuristic: buffer up to 80 bytes or 40ms, forward if buffer forms valid utf8 JSON or timeout. Also add `stream.small_frame_rate` and `stream.reconnect_rate` metrics per-route.

maya: canaryed a patch in staging (buffer 80B/40ms) — reconnects dropped from ~15/min to ~2/min for test clients. p95 latency +7ms.

ellen: add console card on route page: "Stream health" with tiny-frame spikes, reconnect loops, and coalesce latency. Also CLI toggle for rapid rollback.

trace-bot: deploy: edge-proxy/staging canary c-204 started 2026-03-23T11:30:00Z.

diego: caution: heartbeats are tiny by design. Make sure heartbeat pattern (e.g., single `\n` or `\r`) is exempt from coalescing. Also don't log payloads — only hashes + lengths.

maya: noted. follow-ups: @ellen finish PR, @diego add metrics and dashboard, i'll run canary traffic for 2h and report.

ellen: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/ellen/edge-coalesce (WIP). CLI flag `--coalesce-small-frames=false` included.

maya: staging hold 45m so far, looks stable. will update after 120m. :thumbsup:
